problem: Let $f(x)$ be a function with $f(7)=4,{f}^{′}(7)=2,{f}^{″}(7)=-6$ and ${f}^{‴}(7)=-24.$ Which of the following is the third-degree Taylor polynomial for $f(x)$ about $x=7?$
worked_solution:
The third-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=7$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{3}(x) & =f(7)+{f}^{′}(7)(x-7)+\frac{{f}^{″}(7)}{2!}(x-7)^{2}+\frac{{f}^{‴}(7)}{3!}(x-7)^{3} \\  & =f(7)+{f}^{′}(7)(x-7)+\frac{{f}^{″}(7)}{2}(x-7)^{2}+\frac{{f}^{‴}(7)}{6}(x-7)^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We have been given the following set of values: 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(7) & =4 \\ {f}^{′}(7) & =2 \\ {f}^{″}(7) & =-6 \\ {f}^{‴}(7) & =-24.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the given values into our Taylor polynomial, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{3}(x) & =4+2(x-7)+\frac{(-6)}{2}(x-7)^{2}+\frac{(-24)}{6}(x-7)^{3} \\  & =4+2(x-7)-3(x-7)^{2}-4(x-7)^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
